assumptions.summary: Ignore inflation, deflation, and time value.
Charity seeks educational/social performance rather than profit.
Schools rather than individuals receive grants.
Marginal utility discourages excessive single-school allocation.
Future ROI is predictable from five historical years.
Annual lower/upper bounds can represent practical timing.
Later decisions should consider feedback from chosen schools.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Raw UID and Scorecard files are joined; non-operating/HCM2 and high-null rows are removed.
Binary and related attributes are merged; location and low-contribution fields are deleted.
Ten missing ROI variables are filled from 18 integral school descriptors.
Five clusters fill missing values by within-cluster means; all attributes are min-max normalized.
Output uses salary, retention, repayment, and enhancement; Input uses net price; Urgency uses Pell, federal loan, and debt.
Basic model reports 14 selected schools and charts their factors/allocation.
Time-series model lists year-indexed investments and an allocation table.
Donor letter lists 16 schools for the successive five-year plan.

The schedule is tested under risk, school-count, and policy alternatives.
Sensitivity and limitations are translated into future data requests and donor communication.

language_observations.summary: Reusable human writing moves center on staged repair, subjective-choice disclosure, horizon-triggered Grey modeling, policy practicality objections, future repair requests, and donor translation.
the Summary compresses a data-to-donation route: Move from dirty institutional data through repair, ROI, one-year/five-year allocation, sensitivity, and a bounded recommendation.
a concrete information problem triggers staged repair: Use scale, mixed types, and missingness to justify screening, K-means fill, and normalization before analysis.
a policy objective becomes measurable output components: Translate educational/social benefit into salary, retention, repayment, and enhancement before weighting.
missing data are repaired through similarity: Name alternatives, define integral descriptors, cluster schools, and fill each missing column by within-cluster means.
an internal fit statistic chooses the clustering count: Compare candidate K values, maximize R², then use the selected partition for imputation.
input imbalance triggers a correction index: When net price dominates the ratio, add α and state its selected value before using corrected Input.
social mission adds an urgency multiplier to ROI: Start from financial ROI, add charitable need, choose Pell/loan/debt indicators, and weight them.
subjective weighting is defended against false objectivity: Acknowledge AHP subjectivity, argue objective weights may miss practice, and use a consistency check.
a proxy difference becomes education enhancement: Use normalized post-graduation salary minus pre-entry SAT, then reweight schools without SAT.
a longer donation horizon triggers Grey prediction: Move from one-year ROI to five-year planning, use GM(1,1), and extrapolate past observations.
a risk ratio turns dispersion into an allocation constraint: Define salary coefficient of variation and carry it into the MILP risk bound.
the decision rule precedes the recommendation table: State variables, objective, constraints, and solver before publishing schools and amounts.
a time extension adds indexed decisions and repeated constraints: Introduce year-indexed variables, annual bounds, and a five-year result table after the basic model.
a sensitivity curve is read into a threshold claim: Vary acceptable risk, read the rising-then-flat curve, and identify a plateau.
a non-monotone school-count curve identifies a practical optimum: Vary selected-school count, locate the peak, and compare it with the allowed range.
the best unconstrained policy is rejected as impractical: Compare distribution policies, expose extreme early concentration, and choose a near-best bounded policy.
future work turns candid defects into data requests: Name intuitive/result defects, then request experts, subject/student detail, real data, and peer-charity information.
strengths and weaknesses form a compact audit ledger: Pair integrity, technical support, fusion, and flexibility with data, subjectivity, assumption, and dynamics weaknesses.
the conclusion compresses a method stack with caveats: Restate processing, ROI, basic/time-series models, and methods while preserving a qualified assessment.
the donor letter translates the index into a monitored handoff: Explain mission, before/after ability, ROI components, model stack, recommendations, and feedback caveat.

source_quality.summary: All 24 physical pages were read in order and visually reviewed. The paper moves from data screening and K-means repair through a subjective ROI index, Grey forecasting, risk-aware basic/time-series MILP, sensitivity, explicit weaknesses, future data requests, and a donor handoff.

decisions: which schools enter the candidate set, how to value output/need/cost, which schools receive grants, when to invest, and how to update with feedback

title: An Educational Donation Mechanism Based On Data Insight
unresolved_questions: Printed Contents and headers end at 22 while the physical PDF has 24 pages with a donor letter.
The basic result names 14 schools while the donor letter foregrounds 16 five-year schools without an explicit bridge.
The 7,805 to 2,978 to about 2,700 screening counts have no frozen row-level inclusion ledger or recall audit.
Operational/HCM2 deletion and >50-percent-null deletion can encode policy and missingness selection bias.
One K-means partition is assumed applicable to every missing output column.
K=5 is chosen from an internal R2 range without external imputation or downstream sensitivity.
EER subtracts normalized salary and SAT as if commensurate learning gain without construct or causal validation.
AHP consistency indices check matrix coherence, not importance validity.
Alpha, urgency direction, and urgency weights are subjective and lack elicitation or uncertainty.
ROI combines salary, rates, debt, and net price without a full dimensional/welfare ledger.
Grey prediction uses five historical years and reports no forecast error or residual diagnostics.
Risk uses only salary coefficient of variation and omits model, implementation, and beneficiary risks.
MILP uses fixed school statistics and omits inflation, time value, and donation feedback.
Basic and five-year recommendation counts are not fully reconciled (14 versus 16).
Result charts and tables lack solver trace, seed, optimality gap, raw feasible solution, and uncertainty.
Policy 4 is rejected on an informal early-year allocation criterion; practicality is not formalized.
One-way risk, school-count, and policy sensitivity does not establish joint decision stability.
Validity claims exceed descriptive internal plots and policy comparisons.
The donor letter gives only a brief feedback caveat rather than an explicit monitoring/update protocol.
No code, raw data snapshot, imputation mask, PCA/AHP workbook, Grey residuals, or MILP certificate is released.
